mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authentication of Articles of Association (Statuts) before a Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial deed (domestic act; no apostille required in Luxembourg)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent entity / sole shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial register in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the issuing state is not a Hague member, consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Attestation of the corporate shareholder or parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registrar / Companies Registry in jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney to execute incorporation formalities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport / national identity copies of all managers and ultimate beneficial owners

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy by Luxembourg notary; where necessary apostilled or legalized

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, managers, directors and UBOs against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignement Financier), CSSF AML/CFT data, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, UK HMT sanctions, and global PEP databases. UBO piercing must be performed through intermediate entities, trusts and nominees until a natural person controller is identified. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, FATF high-risk jurisdictions, and claims of nominee representation; any match requires escalation to the compliance officer and potentially a refusal of incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal (www.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be based on a Latin-script representation; if the desired name uses non-Latin characters or is a brand mark not in Latin characters, a transliterated Latin-character version must be filed with the RCS. The legal form must appear in the name as 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. The name must be distinctive, not identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and shall not mislead the public as to the nature, scale or public connection of the company. All corporate documents and the notarial deed are prepared in French; English and German are accepted for auxiliary submission.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Luxembourg (when used to imply official patronage or state sponsorship)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejection notification from the RCS must be appealed by a lawyer admitted in Luxembourg. An application for annulment/reformation shall be filed with the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification. The applicant may simultaneously file a new name-reservation request after amending the name or choose to maintain the original name until final ruling. If the name is refused on substantive grounds (e.g., legal-form suffix missing or misleading similarity), the applicant must correct the non-compliance and submit a fresh request. No administrative extension of the initial 60-day reservation window is available after expiration unless a new reservation is made.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if offered by a duly licensed and supervised domiciliation / corporate service provider and the company has sufficient substance for tax and AML/CFT purposes. The RCS requires a full physical address within Luxembourg and does not register a P.O. Box. For a market-research SaaS platform that does not require a regulated license, a virtual office is accepted at the pre-incorporation stage; however, full substance must be established (should the entity apply for VAT, employ staff, or hold an IP/registration position) or tax authorities may disregard residence status.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 10% to 20% annual likelihood; increases to 50-70% if the company claims Luxembourg residence while performing management offshore, holds a large intangible asset, or seeks VAT registration with no local staff.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended, notably Articles 180 to 190 governing Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) filed electronically with the RCS via the LBR online filing platform
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash on formation; the amount must be deposited and blocked in a Luxembourg-licensed bank account pending registration (escrow release occurs only upon RCS certificate issuance).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation documents and the statutory capital subscription of EUR 12,000 evidenced by the capital blocked account certificate are hereby ratified and approved in full. RESOLVED: That the registered office shall be established at [registered office address], Luxembourg, and the appointed notary is instructed to file the application with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED: That [Name] is appointed sole Manager with full authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and bind the company. RESOLVED: That the Manager is authorized to complete all tax, VAT, and social security registrations and take any ancillary action required to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Reservation and Pre-Formation Compliance Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS Name Reservation Module (online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the LBR online portal, indicating the desired SARL corporate name and the intended ISIC scope (market research and consumer polling). Provide a signed mandate and proof of identity of the founder. Verify absence of identical or confusingly similar names in the RCS index and confirm that the name does not contravene Luxembourg public order rules.
required_dossiers: Copy of founder's valid passport or identity card
Signed power of attorney if using a local representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name conflicts with an existing trademark or corporate name, amend the proposed name and refile; the registry will hold priority for the first valid submission upon payment of the statutory reservation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Blocked Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed credit institution established in Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Approach a Luxembourg bank with a draft capital deposit instruction. Open a dedicated account in the name of the 'SARL in formation', transfer the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital, and obtain a 'blocked capital certificate' (attestation de blocage de capital) confirming the funds are unavailable for withdrawal until presentation of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Letter of instruction from beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced peer-to-peer business model explanations, submit a supplementary ISIC 7320 activity description; if any correction is required, adjust the bank instruction and obtain a revised blockage certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) holding an active commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the final Articles of Incorporation, capital blockage certificate, and name reservation receipt to the notary. The notary will verify the legality of the corporate form (SARL), read the statutes aloud, obtain signatures of all subscriber shareholders, and execute an authentic deed (acte notarié).
required_dossiers: Capital blockage certificate from Luxembourg bank
Draft statuts containing corporate governance, registered office, and manager appointment clauses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a conflict with mandatory corporate law provisions, amend the relevant clauses and re-execute the deed on the same day; no fee is repeated for substantive legal changes if the notary has not yet filed the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Acte de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) electronically through the LBR portal, together with the statutory form for RCS registration (Formulaire A - Société à responsabilité limitée). Disclose the legal form, registered office address, object, subscribed capital, managers, and any beneficial ownership information. Pay the registration fee and await issuance of an RCS extract (extrait) and registration number.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registration fee
Declaration of non-conviction / deputation for manager(s)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a substantive query concerning the corporate object or capital, submit a corrective memorandum and any notarial rectificative deed within 15 days; the RCS will suspend the application until the documentation is compliant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium and Post-Registration Governance Formalties
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / Government Electronic Resa (Recueil électronique des sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, ensure the statutory corporate data (formation, governors, registered office) is published in RESA as required by law. Hold the first board/shareholder meeting formally appointing the manager, approve the initial registered office lease, and complete the national register of beneficial owners filing via the LBR portal. Confirm VAT and social security registrations are initiated with the Luxembourg tax office (Administration des contributions directes) and the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is rejected due to formatting inconsistencies, correct the register extract and resubmit through the LBR portal; any missing beneficial ownership disclosure is immediately cured by filing a supplementary declaration within 1 month following the registry request.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) - General Directorate for Business Concessions (not applicable, no mandatory sectoral license for market research SaaS platform)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific operating license is mandated under Luxembourg law for ISIC 7320 consumer polling / market-research SaaS activities; government permits are limited to standard real estate occupancy, data protection, and occupational safety clearances.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement - Luxembourg Environmental Protection Administration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category G (service/tertiary activity) under the Luxembourg environmental impact assessment catalogue; no full EIA required as the platform uses no industrial plant, hazardous processes, or point-source discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the core digital service; where contained office premises are used, the operator must comply with Luxembourg waste management obligations (Regulation on waste separation) and, if a local server room is present, with technical building ventilation standards respecting ordinary ambient air discharges associated with consumer electronics.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance for any physical office premises must be obtained from the Fire and Rescue Service (Service d'incendie et de secours - SIS) via the commune's building permit certificate; structural load confirmation for the office floor is issued by the municipal 'Commune' urbanism department following a simplified technical review. Workplace safety clearance is issued by the Luxembourg Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) after verification that the registered office space meets basic health and safety requirements for seated logistical/administrative staff, including emergency exits, electrical safety, and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct and corporate income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified business portal: Guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity engaging in taxable activities in Luxembourg must appoint a fiscal representative (unless established within the EU) and submit the Luxembourg VAT registration application via MyGuichet.lu to the AEDT, providing proof of EU establishment, entity constitutive documents, and expected turnover. Where Luxembourg-source income other than VAT arises, the foreign entity must also register with the ACD using the standard non-resident business registration procedure and obtain a Luxembourg national identification number (numéro d'identification).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Luxembourg SARL is a resident company taxed at corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax on worldwide income, subject to treaty and territorial relief; no tax-exempt zone or pass-through classification applies to a standard commercial SARL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box or entity-classification election regime for direct tax. A SARL may elect VAT grouping under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT law with related Luxembourg entities, may apply for advance tax agreements with the ACD on transfer pricing or hybrid transactions, and must implement domestic and EU rules on hybrid mismatch arrangements (ATAD) with no elective opt-out for mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No annual turnover threshold for non-resident suppliers; any taxable supply in Luxembourg triggers registration. A Luxembourg resident small enterprise may qualify for the annual VAT exemption of €35,000 (excluding VAT) under Article 57 of the VAT law, except for certain businesses and supplies. Intra-Community distance sales of goods benefit from the €10,000 pan-EU distance-selling threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based reporting, or digital stamping is currently imposed by the AEDT. Public-sector (B2G) electronic invoicing is mandatory via PEPPOL BIS 3.0; B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and is to follow EN 16931, with future mandatory requirements planned under EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to supplies exported outside the EU, provided the exporter obtains a customs export declaration and evidence of physical removal from the EU within 90 days. Services: market research and comparable services supplied to a taxable person established outside Luxembourg and outside the EU are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (reverse-charge jurisdiction in the customer's country). B2B services to EU taxable customers are taxable where the customer is established; B2C services may be zero-rated where effective use and enjoyment lies outside the EU and the customer is outside the EU, otherwise the standard Luxembourg rate applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill
Proof of physical removal from EU (certified export document)
Bank or payment system records showing cross-border receipt (e.g., Inward Remittance Certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively disallow zero-rating where the exporter fails to retain the entire export dossier. Late VAT or wrongly claimed zero-rating attracts legal interest at 0.6% per month plus administrative fines; deliberate or fraudulent misuse of zero-rating may lead to criminal sanctions and full clawback of unreported VAT. Records supporting export zero-rating must be preserved for a minimum of 10 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); banking and financial-sector supervision additionally performed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member state; the euro is fully convertible and no exchange-control restrictions apply to current or capital account transactions under Articles 63-65 TFEU. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to the standard 15% dividend withholding tax, which is reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or the Luxembourg participation exemption conditions (minimum 10% shareholding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition price, 12-month holding period) are satisfied. No ministerial authorization or prior BCL approval is required for dividend distribution, loan repayment, or capital repatriation, provided statutory corporate-law solvency tests are met.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory obligation exists in Luxembourg to surrender, convert, or maintain export proceeds in any mandated currency. Export receipts may be retained indefinitely in EUR or foreign currency, and no minimum conversion ratio applies. The only compliance duty is statistical: cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 per transaction must be declared to the BCL for balance-of-payments reporting purposes, and the entity must retain underlying commercial documentation supporting each declaration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with FX and Hedging Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is High for low-value, high-volume payout rails, subject to PSD2 legal constraints. A non-EEA EMI (e.g., FCA-licensed Wise) may provide payment services in Luxembourg only through a valid EEA/EEA-passported entity such as Wise Payments Europe S.A. or another CSSF-recognised EMI. The target rails, PayPal Mass Payout and Wise, are operationally viable for micro-payouts to consumer panelists, but a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank account remains mandatory as the primary treasury nester for subscribed capital, dividend capacity, and statutory reserve maintenance; the EMI route is supplementary, not structural.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CSSF post-COVID guidance permits remote video-based customer due diligence for Low_Risk_Standard corporate profiles, but in current market practice most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one director or an authorized signatory holding a power of attorney to complete an in-person KYC interview at onboarding; remote onboarding is available selectively (e.g., at BGL BNP Paribas and BIL) where the UBO chain is fully transparent and all identification documents are notarised and apostilled. At least one natural-person director must present valid government-issued identification; where no director is physically in Luxembourg, a Luxembourg-resident authorized agent may be required for service-of-process purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: SARL owned through intermediate non-EU holding companies with non-transparent shareholder registers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) official extract, notarised corporate organization chart, apostilled passport copies of all ultimate beneficial owners, source-of-wealth declarations, and an explanatory board-minute letter confirming the chain of ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity mass disbursements: PayPal Mass Payout and Wise API payouts to thousands of consumer panelists flagged as possible pass-through or money-velocity risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panelist KYC and identity-verification records, batch payout audit reports, underlying survey/panel-participation contracts, payout policy documentation, an AML/CFT procedure manual, EU/UN sanctions screening results, and CEO attestation of commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS bluebird revenues with counterparties located in medium- or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Customer due diligence files, sanctions-screening outputs, source-of-funds trails tied to executed invoices, acceptable-use policy and refusal-of-service records for sanctioned or restricted geographies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uncharacteristic liquidity patterns caused by PayPal reserve holds or settlement mismatches between payin and payout cycles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PayPal settlement and reserve statements, bank-reconciliation reports, board-approved treasury policy governing liquidity thresholds, and a bank reference letter confirming historical transaction behavior.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder capital injections route via SWIFT MT103 from a bank account held in the shareholder's own name, using the BIC and SARL's IBAN at the Luxembourg receiving bank; the declared purpose code must identify the capital contribution / direct investment. All inbound transfers exceeding EUR 12,500 per transaction are captured by BCL balance-of-payments statistical declarations; the compliance file must include the board resolution authorising share issuance, the notarised subscription deed, proof of payment into the capital account, and the BCL declaration reference number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU-zone trade settlements execute via SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001); non-EU supplier payments execute via SWIFT MT103 with explicit remittance information; where documentary payment terms are required, a Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) is available but rarely optimal for a low-risk SaaS/market-research services model. Panelist micropayments settle through PayPal Mass Payout and Wise payout APIs, supported by daily EUR/USD netting, automated reconciliation against the ledger, and independent bank-account settlement buffers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forward (FXA) executed under ISDA/CSA with a Luxembourg bank
EUR/USD FX swap (FXS) for rolling near-dated liquidity conversion
EUR/USD OTC vanilla currency option or zero-cost collar for downside protection with capped upside
Cross-currency swap (EUR vs USD) for treasury liability and interest-rate-aligned hedging
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) strictly limited to underlying exposures in non-convertible or restricted currencies (e.g., USD/BRL, USD/ARS) where physical settlement is legally prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registration data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (via eJustice eDesk)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due each year no later than the last day of the month in which the RCS registration anniversary falls
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an infringement notice, possible court-ordered coercive fine, and ultimately administrative strike-off (radiation d'office).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (eJustice electronic filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end; a 31 December year-end must be filed by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects directors to court summons and a coercive fine up to EUR 10,000; persistent non-compliance may result in administrative strike-off and criminal fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (registered beneficial owner data)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), managed by the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm beneficial-owner data is a criminal offence punishable by fines of EUR 500 to EUR 10,000, with additional administrative penalties and strike-off risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, the initial deadline is 31 May of the following tax year; a filing extension is available on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing leads to default tax assessment, late-interest of 0.6% per month, a late-filing penalty of up to 5% of assessed tax, and eventual forced collection/execution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit applies if the SARL exceeds, on two consecutive financial years, at least two of the three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (substantively aligned with EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU) is the default statutory-accounting framework; IFRS may be applied voluntarily and is required for the consolidated accounts of listed Luxembourg entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Sarl must annually reconfirm its registered beneficial-owner data with the RBE by 31 March. Every shareholding transfer during the year must first be recorded in the corporate register of members and internally documented; a UBO update must be filed with the RBE within one month of the transfer, and the annual confirmation then verifies the continued accuracy of aggregate shareholding as at the confirmation date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 2,000 per year for registered office / fiduciary agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 9,000 per year for a typical small/medium Sarl statutory audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline in Luxembourg City for FY2025: 17% national corporate income tax (CIT), plus a 7% unemployment fund contribution calculated on the CIT, plus 6.75% municipal business tax (communal multiplier of 225% applied to the 3% base rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime: 80% exemption of qualifying net IP income, yielding an effective combined rate of approximately 4.99%. Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividend income and capital gains where the SARL holds at least 10% of the subsidiary's share capital (or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million) for at least 12 consecutive months. R&D tax credit: refundable credit of 30% on qualifying R&D expenditure up to EUR 3,000,000 and 20% on the excess. Notional interest deduction (NID) available on increases in equity, subject to the 2019-reform refinements. A minimum CIT of EUR 3,215 per tax year applies to the ordinary operating SARL; higher minimums under Luxembourg City wealth-tax practices do not apply because the entity is an active trading company rather than a financial holding vehicle.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_note: Unlimited carryforward under Luxembourg law; losses may be carried forward indefinitely, although the deduction is limited to 75% of the taxable basis of the year for CIT purposes after 2017 per the Luxembourg loss-compensation cap, and municipal business tax only allows a deduction for losses derived from the same municipality.
corporate_income_tax_regime.minimum_tax_note: EUR 3,215 per year; no minimum income tax exemption for SARLs regardless of turnover.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt foncier) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu using a professional eID (Luxtrust certificate) or by the certified fiscal representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the Model 100 is a single consolidated return covering CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax components for the calendar year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed no later than 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., FY2025 return due 31 December 2026). The Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes, AED) may send a reminder or an official tax-form package; failure to receive the package does not relieve the filing obligation. Quarterly prepayments of income tax are due on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, and 10 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SARL, RCS Luxembourg number, tax file number (matricule d'identification), registered office, legal form, date of incorporation, and contact details of the gérant (manager).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident entity with a Luxembourg permanent establishment, provide the foreign company's home registration particulars, the address of the Luxembourg PE, and an attestation of the PE's effective management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the fiscal year; normally the calendar year for Luxembourg SARLs unless a non-calendar fiscal year has been validly adopted in the articles of association and disclosed to the AED.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the foreign parent applies a non-calendar fiscal year, the Luxembourg PE return must still reconcile to the Luxembourg tax year unless a deviation has been agreed with the AED in advance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets, shareholders' equity, long-term liabilities, short-term liabilities, and separately identified financial instruments. The balance sheet must correspond to the Luxembourg GAAP annual accounts filed with the RCS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must produce a PE carve-out balance sheet showing assets and liabilities attributable to the Luxembourg PE; head-office balances shall not be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover from the consumer-panel platform: survey subscription fees, market-research project revenue, panel data licensing, SaaS access fees, and cross-border commissions. All revenue must be recorded on an accrual basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Luxembourg-source service income to the PE if the contracts are concluded and the services are economically performed in Luxembourg; foreign-source income attributable to the PE remains taxable if the PE is the entrepreneurial centre.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating deductions: employee wages and social security, cloud/SaaS hosting, payment-processing fees of PayPal and Wise, panel remuneration, marketing, subcontracted research costs, rent, depreciation, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses economically borne by the Luxembourg PE; head-office recharges require written intercompany agreements and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items to be re-added (fines, gifts exceeding EUR 125 per recipient, non-documented expenses), the IP-box deduction for qualifying IP, participation-exemption deductions for dividends and capital gains, and the R&D tax-credit computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses supported by local Luxembourg books and vouchers are deductible; treaty-based adjustments must be claimed in the annex to the return, not by direct reduction of the taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Rubric 7 – Taxable base and municipal business tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of commercial taxable income: adjusted result, addition of certain interest, deduction of carried forward losses, and application of the municipal business-tax base rate; the communal multiplier of the commune of business establishment must be entered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the municipality where the PE is established; a PE located in Luxembourg City triggers the 225% multiplier; non-residents pay municipal business tax on the Luxembourg PE share only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Rubric 8 – Minimum income tax and notional interest deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the EUR 3,215 minimum income tax if applicable, and separate election for the notional interest deduction if the SARL increased equity in a qualifying manner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a Luxembourg PE must pay the same minimum income tax on the PE; no NID is available for foreign equity that is not used by the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly prepayments already paid, the R&D tax credit to be offset, and any foreign withholding tax credits eligible under the applicable double-tax treaty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits must be claimed with a completed Form 240 (structure) and supported by a tax residence certificate of the source-country tax administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signature of the gérant or the authorized tax representative; attachment of the statutory financial statements, the transfer-pricing documentation index, and the list of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners where required by the AED.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident gérant must attach a power of attorney in favor of the Luxembourg tax agent; the AED may reject the filing if the beneficial-ownership annex is missing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Model 100 triggers a contravention fine between EUR 25 and EUR 2,500 per breach. Late or non-payment of assessed tax triggers a 10% majoration of the tax and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum) on the arrears. Incomplete or false declarations expose the entity to taxation d'office and to the criminal penalties described in the fatal red flags section.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annex A – Transfer-pricing documentation index (not a standalone return, but a compulsory AED file component filed upon request via MyGuichet or in paper form within 30 days of the AED request).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, contemporaneous; the Master File and Local File are updated by the fiscal-year end and delivered to the AED upon written demand.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No fixed calendar deadline for submission, but the documentation must exist at the time of the tax return and be produced within 30 days of the AED request. Late production triggers the documentation penalty of up to EUR 25,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Organizational chart of the ultimate parent, all group entities, jurisdictions, and the place of the SARL within the group.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg PE of a foreign group must include the complete global structure to let the AED map intra-group flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of all related-party transactions: cross-border service recharges, IP royalties from the survey platform, panel data purchases, and financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transactions with the foreign head office must be described separately from transactions with other group affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the transfer-pricing method, comparability analysis, functional and risk profile (DEMPE) of the Luxembourg operations, and the resulting arm's-length financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg PE's profit attribution must follow the authorized OECD approach and be supported by comparable data from independent market-research firms.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: A benchmarking study or interquartile range of independent comparables justifying the tested party's margin.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Comparables must be adjusted for Luxembourg market conditions and geographic differences if the foreign parent is the tested party.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to produce the TP documentation within 30 days exposes the SARL to the EUR 25,000 administrative fine and shifts the burden of proof to the taxpayer in any transfer-pricing adjustment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends distributed by a resident société de capitaux (SARL) to non-resident shareholders. The rate is reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the shareholder holds at least 10% of the SARL's capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period, or to 0%/5%/15% under applicable double-tax treaties depending on the holding structure; US- and UK-treaty investors typically secure 5% for qualifying 10%+ holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty or EU-directive relief at the moment of distribution, the SARL must obtain and retain: (i) a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) of the shareholder issued by its home tax authority for the relevant tax year; (ii) a declaration of beneficial ownership signed by the shareholder; and (iii) evidence of the 12-month minimum holding commitment. The SARL then files Form 271 (demande en dispense / renonciation à la retenue à la source) with the AED before the dividend distribution date. If withholding has already occurred, the shareholder must file a refund claim on Form 271 within five years of the distribution; the AED examines the economic substance of the recipient under the CJEU Danish Cases and Luxembourg GAAR and denies relief where the shareholder is a letterbox vehicle.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on outbound royalty payments, regardless of the residence of the recipient; however, excessive royalties to related non-resident entities are recharacterized as constructive dividends, subject to the 15% WHT. Interest: ordinary commercial interest is free of Luxembourg WHT. Article 115 LIR imposes a 20% WHT on interest paid by a Luxembourg resident to a related non-resident company that is not subject to a comparable tax and is not protected by an EU/treaty provision where the economically relevant lender test (third-party funding test) is not satisfied.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR. Local File and Master File obligations arise where the Luxembourg SARL concludes aggregate related-party transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 in a fiscal year; the Master File is mandatory where the consolidated group revenue of the ultimate parent exceeds EUR 750,000,000. Country-by-Country Reporting applies at group level where the consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750,000,000, with automatic exchange through the OECD framework. Documentation must be delivered to the AED within 30 days of request; non-production triggers a fine of up to EUR 25,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply an offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations statute (as in UAE or similar regimes); the equivalent substance requirements flow from the GAAR in Article 6 of the Steueranpassungsgesetz (abuse of forms), the 2019 Luxembourg transfer-pricing framework, the EU ATAD minimum substance standards, the proposed EU Unshell (ATAD 3) directive, and the beneficial-ownership jurisprudence of the CJEU. For this consumer-panel survey platform, the operational reality of premises, employees, the DEMPE function over the survey software, and the local decision-making of the gérant will satisfy the doctrine; a letterbox SARL without staff, office, or local contracts would be denied treaty benefits, have its income reattributed to the foreign shareholder, and face a 100% recapture of tax incentives.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.documentation_reference: The AED applies the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines 2022 and the Luxembourg Circular LIR n° 56/1 – 56/1ter; the arm's-length range must be applied with interquartile statistical support.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally concealing or under-declaring cross-border survey and market-research revenues earned through the Luxembourg SARL; booking income to a zero-tax affiliate while the SARL retains the entrepreneurial risk; fabricating costs for non-existent subcontracted panels; or destroying accounting records before the five-year legal retention period expires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Article 396 of the Steueranpassungsgesetz and the Luxembourg anti-fraud law of 6 July 2016: imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and a fine up to EUR 250,000 for individuals; legal persons are additionally liable to fines up to EUR 1,000,000. The tax administration reassesses the suppressed income, applies the 10% majoration, charges monthly interest of 0.6%, and the fraudulent documents can be used to extend the statute of limitations to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and any de facto director who signed or directed the false return are personally subject to the criminal fines and imprisonment; courts routinely issue travel bans, asset freezes, and confiscation orders. Directors may also be held civilly liable in solidum for the company's tax shortfall where the evasion results from their intentional wrongful act.
